newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australia rice exports to jump in 96/97 - ABARE.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australia rice exports to jump in 96/97 - ABARE.

text.p: Australian (paddy) rice exports were forecast to rise by 50 percent in the year to June 30, 1997 after falling short of expectations in 1995/96, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said.
In its September quarter bulletin, ABARE forecast exports to rise to 717,000 tonnes, but revised down estimates for 1995/96 to a preliminary 477,000 from a forecast for 607,000.

Depending on the availability of irrigation water, ABARE expected near capacity plantings in 1996/97 which, at average yields, would produce a record 1.3 million tonnes of paddy rice up from a downward revised 951,000 tonnes in 1995/96.
The average return to Australian rice growers was forecast to be A$202 per tonne in 1996/97, 3.8 percent lower than in 1995/96 and 13 percent short of the record set in 1993/94.
Plantings were expected to cover 150,000 hectares in 1996/97, up marginally from 149,000 the year before.

World prices were expected to decline slightly as the tight supply/demand situation for other food grains eases, ABARE said. World production was forecast to rise 1.6 percent to a record 377 million tonnes reflecting the generally favourable monsoon this year. Among the major exporters, only India was expected to have larger amounts of rice available for export.
